chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: This paper investigates the feasibility of deploying quadruped walking robots for the automation of work in roof environments. ... Roof environments represent a novel and unexplored use case, combining high safety risks for human workers with repetitive, strenuous tasks that could benefit from robotic assistance.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately states the research problem of investigating the feasibility of using quadruped robots to automate hazardous and repetitive tasks in roof environments.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: A dedicated test rig of a roof’s surface was designed to evaluate the baseline performance of a commercial quadruped, the Unitree Go2, in this new environment.
chk_method.reason: The poster accurately describes the method of designing a dedicated roof surface test rig to evaluate the baseline performance of the Unitree Go2.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: Test rig: An adjustable test rig of a roof environment was developed using the Frankfurter Pfanne, the most common roof tile in Germany.
chk_data.reason: The poster accurately identifies the Frankfurter Pfanne roof tiles used as the surface material on the test rig.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Three core skills of the Go2 (software 1.4.4) were examined, each repeated ten times: 1. Balancing: robot placed facing uphill at 0° incline, gradually increased until balance was lost. 2. Get-up/lie-down: assessed on progressively steeper inclines in three orientations (uphill, downhill, sideways); success = completing both actions. 3. Incline walking: repeated ascents of increasingly steep slopes while measuring slippage with OptiTrack markers at the sides of the ball feet. ... All trials were controlled via Python using a WebRTC implementation for high repeatability. The robot was set to standard walking mode with a target speed of 1.0 m/s, a realistic speed for real-world applications.
chk_setup.reason: The poster accurately details the experimental setup, including the three core skills examined, the Python control, and the target speed of 1.0 m/s.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Experiments revealed that standard ball feet are inherently inadequate for locomotion on sloped roofs: slippage increased quadratically with incline angle, get-up and lie-down sequences were only possible on small inclines, and critical failures already occurred regularly on moderate inclines of 25°.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster accurately states the primary quantitative result regarding quadratic slippage and critical failures at 25°.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Standing on incline: critical angle (27.58 ± 0.72)°. ... Get-up/lie-down: full success only at low inclines — up to 11.0° for head-up and head-down, up to 7.0° sideways.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster accurately reports the secondary results, including the critical standing angle of 27.58 ± 0.72° and the get-up/lie-down success limits.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: Manufacturer claims of slope-climbing up to 40° were not achieved under test conditions.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster accurately compares the robot's performance against the manufacturer's slope-climbing claim of 40°.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Without appropriate adaptations, quadrupeds are not yet capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately states the main conclusion that unmodified quadrupeds are not currently capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Limitations: ... all tests were conducted under ideal conditions without debris, vegetation, weather or payloads.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster accurately lists the limitation that experiments were conducted under ideal conditions without debris, vegetation, weather, or payloads.
